taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: a perennial herb from 8 to 18 inches tall (0.2-0.45 m).

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: stems mostly solitary or few together, 1-6 dm. tall.

traits.life_span.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: perennial from elongate, mostly nearly naked rhizomes.

traits.woodiness.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 418, Arnica: fibrous-rooted perennial herbs from a rhizome or caudex.

traits.leaf_habit.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it: the leafy stems die back each winter.

traits.perennation.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: perennial from elongate, mostly nearly naked rhizomes which may be branched.

traits.rhizome_habit.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: rootstock underground, slender, long-creeping, with paired buds.

traits.clonal.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: in some localities it is the dominant species and may be found in almost pure stands; grows from running rootstocks.

traits.rosette.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: basal leaves sometimes produced on separate short shoots; the flowering stems leafy.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 418, Arnica: leaves simple, opposite, or the reduced uppermost ones occasionally alternate.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: cauline leaves commonly 3-14 cm. long.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: cauline leaves commonly 1.5-8 cm. wide.

traits.petiole_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cauline leaves sessile or short-petiolate, the petiole up to about 2 cm, as in the photos; Abrams (1960 p. 423): sessile or petiolate.

traits.leaf_shape.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 423, Arnica latifolia: lance-elliptic or generally broader, rarely cordate; the Range Plant Handbook (p. W25): egg-shaped, rounded or oval.

traits.leaf_margin.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: usually sharply toothed on margins; Abrams (1960 p. 423): more or less toothed.

traits.leaf_hairs.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: the leaves, stems and involucre smooth or nearly free from hair.

traits.inflorescence.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: flower heads usually several (cymose), on slender stalks from axils of upper leaves; Abrams: heads 1-3 or sometimes more; drawn as three.

traits.capitulum_kind.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: outside (ray) flowers petal-like, yellow, strap-shaped; center (disk) flowers small, numerous, yellow, tubular.

traits.ray_florets.note: Flora of North America vol. 21 p. 367, 375, 376 (eFloras, read 2026-10-19), Arnica latifolia: ray florets 8-15; corollas yellow.

traits.ray_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: rays 1.2 cm to 2.5 cm long, as in the photos.

traits.ray_apex.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: rays usually 7-veined, 3-toothed at tip.

traits.ray_colour.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: showy, bright-yellow, sunflowerlike flower heads; sRGB by eye from the photos.

traits.disc_colour.note: Range Plant Handbook (1937) p. W25, Arnica latifolia: disk flowers yellow; deeper yellow-orange in the photos; sRGB by eye.

traits.involucre_height_m.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 424, Arnica latifolia: involucre mostly 10-18 mm. high.

traits.involucre_diameter_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: involucre 1 cm to 2 cm across, turbinate to subhemispheric (Abrams 1960 p. 423).

traits.fruit_type.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 424, Arnica latifolia: achenes generally glabrous; pappus white, barbellate.

traits.flowering_months.note: Abrams and Ferris vol. 4 (1960) p. 424, Arnica latifolia: June-Aug.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: achenes ripe in August and September.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: patches of slender stems with two to four pairs of broad, toothed, bright green leaves, each stem bearing one to three bright yellow daisy heads with toothed rays.

generator.params.note: Set by hand for broadleaf arnica from its sources and the photos the traits cite: the herb program's structure (stems, nodes, basal leaves, how the flowers are borne). The rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.35 m tall at 4 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

sources.title: Project After contributors: hand-set species values

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added for the Mount Rainier subalpine meadow scene (Paradise, 2026-10-19): sizes and forms from Abrams (vols. 2 to 4) and the Range Plant Handbook where it treats the species, counts and colours from iNaturalist photos.
